title: Kernel morning liftoff log — Kyla
quick_todos: 1) Reproduce eviction w/ small seq lengths locally (use trace mode)
2) Add perf counters around KV write/read paths (counters: kv_writes, kv_reads, kv_evictions)
3) Draft rollback plan for model-7b quantized variant if spike recurs
4) Pair with Diego on canary rollout settings (batching thresholds)
5) Post short note to #runtime-ops summarizing mitigation steps
body:
2026-03-13 morning capture — quick log of observations from overnight and immediate next steps.

Context:
- Overnight we saw a handful of p99+ latency spikes across a small subset of model-7b quantized nodes (region: us-west2) around 04:13 UTC. Alerts: latency-slo-p99 triggered, then auto-fallback to model-7b-fp16 for ~6 minutes.
- Suspected correlated increase in KV cache evictions (based on reduced cache hit ratio in console).

Raw timeline (from prom + logs):
- 04:12:25 UTC: steady state, p95 ~ 62ms, p99 ~ 210ms
- 04:13:07 UTC: first small burst of requests with longer sequences (avg seq len ~ 1024, up from typical 256)
- 04:13:12 UTC: kv-cache eviction rate spikes (evictions/min +380%)
- 04:13:18 UTC: p99 jumps to ~1.2s on affected pods; autoscaler/fallback triggers at 04:14:03
- 04:19:00 UTC: metrics return to baseline, no OOM or GPU resets in node logs.

Observations and quick hypotheses:
- OBS1: Burst seems tied to spike in sequence length distribution (customer batch job or unusual user pattern). The quantized path for model-7b appears much more sensitive to large KV churn.
- OBS2: Eviction pattern looks like aggressive eager eviction rather than LRU/age-based — suspects: race in update path or miscomputed cost for entries with long position ranges.
- HYP1: When sequence_len > 512, the cache insert path does extra metadata (segment markers) that may bypass cheap fast-path and hit a slower lockful codepath — causing tail latency and a downstream backpressure.
- HYP2: A bug in the recent fast-kv PR (PR #988) where we moved from per-shard mutex -> coarse global lock under certain conditions (edge case: >512 tokens). If so, this explains why only quantized variant (higher memory/per token bookkeeping) shows spike.

Commands I ran (notes):
- kubectl -n serving logs pod/serving-7b-q-3f2 --since=20m | grep -i eviction | tail -n 50
- docker exec -it runtime-debug /bin/bash; perf record -e cycles:u -p <pid> -- sleep 10; perf report --stdio
- curl \"https://console.redwood.internal/api/metrics?query=kv_cache_evictions%7Bmodel%3D\"model-7b\"%7D&start=2026-03-13T04:00:00Z&end=2026-03-13T04:30:00Z\"

Quick local repro plan:
- Use small repro script that ramps sequence lengths: 128 -> 256 -> 512 -> 1024 in 30s windows; dispatch to a single quantized instance locally (docker-compose dev image) while profiling.
- Enable TRACE_KV env var (inject trace headers) to log insert path decisions.
- Instrument kv counters via /metrics endpoint in dev build.

Immediate mitigations applied (overnight by SRE):
- Increased model-7b quantized cache capacity by 20% for us-west2 (hotfix), reduced eviction rate.
- Adjusted fallback threshold lower temporarily so more requests route to fp16 when latency spikes begin.
- Created incident note in JIRA-RT-2421 with initial triage.

Next actions (owner/ETA):
- Diego: add eviction counters and per-path lock timing (ETA: 2026-03-15)
- Samir: run canary with PR#988 reverted on one pool to test if evictions stop (ETA: 2026-03-14 morning)
- Me (Kyla): write short playbook for oncall to bump cache capacity + lower fallback threshold (ETA: today EOD)
- Mina: correlate customer request traces to find originating job (if internal) (ETA: 2026-03-13 midday)

Notes for follow-up experiments:
- Compare behavior of quantized vs fp16 under synthetic long-seq bursts; measure avg lock hold time in each.
- Run micro-batch size variation: micro-batch 1 vs 8 vs 16 under same seq-length distribution; see if batching reduces eviction pressure because of reuse.
- Test enabling prefix-sharing cache mode (experimental) — might reduce inserts by coalescing overlapping prefixes. Risk: correctness for streaming scenarios needs review.

Misc small TODOs and reminders:
- Submit small perf PR to add counter: kv_write_latency_ms_bucket (histogram) — useful for p99 triage.
- Update confluence page with quick mitigation steps (link in linked_artifacts)
- Draft a customer-facing note if we identify a particular external job causing burst (coordinate with CS).

Open questions I want to discuss in standup:
- Is the fallback policy too aggressive in returning to slower variants (we lost some accuracy-sensitive requests)?
- Is there appetite to revert PR#988 if canary proves clean (cost vs stability tradeoff)?
- Should we add an automatic sequence-length detector to route very long sequences to fp16 variant proactively?

Raw logs snippets (kept short):
[04:13:12] kv_cache evict shard=7 count=142 reason=capacity_reclaim
[04:13:12] kv_cache insert shard=7 key=pos_... len=1024 path=fast-path=false lock=global
[04:13:18] latency p99=1210ms pod=serving-7b-q-3f2

Personal note: keep the repro lightweight — running full model on dev is slow/expensive, use shorter context with mocked KV metadata when possible. Also avoid mass canary changes without rollback documented.

End of morning liftoff log. Will paste into incident and follow up after pairing session with Diego at 10:30 PT.
